newsitem.title: USA: Baldwin Piano to cut debt by $25 mln.
newsitem.headline: Baldwin Piano to cut debt by $25 mln.

text.p: Baldwin Piano and Organ Co said Wednesday it would reduce its debt by about $25 million by phasing out consignment sales.
The company, which had outstanding debt of about $39 million at the end of the first quarter, said the phase-out would also accelerate cash flow and income recognition at Baldwin.
It said it expected its measures to "produce a substantial one-time increase in sales and earnings" as its dealers ended their reliance on consignment financing.
The company said it would help dealers obtain lower-cost financing for their inventories.
It said it had created a program with Deutche Financial Services of Anaheim, California, to help reduce financing costs for nearly all of its dealers.
"Our strategic plan to build shareholder value is moving ahead right on schedule and phasing out consignment is an important part of that plan," it said.
"It is a win win situation for Baldwin and its dealers. Our dealers get favorable financing and we get sharply reduced debt and interest expense and lower administrative costs," it added.
Baldwin Piano & Organ Co makes accoustic pianos and other keyboard instruments.
